Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The unemployment rate is 7.3%, which points to roughly mid-to-late 2013 (it was 7.3% in August and September 2013, then 7.0% in November). The 10-year yield at 2.64% fits late 2013 as well.

Gold's 12-month return of -24.5% and its 1m return of -5.7% suggest a month with a gold drop. Gold fell in 2013, with 6m at -15.9%. The 3m return of +5.8% suggests a rise from the June lows, and October 2013 fits that.

Unemployment would be 7.3% for the October report, which was published in November. Headline CPI of 1.52% matches September 2013 (1.2%) or October (1.0%) less well, though the snapshot may use a different measure. Core CPI at 1.77% is close to the actual 1.7%.

The 10-year yield at 2.64% matches the October 2013 average of about 2.55%. The 3m change in unemployment is -0.3 (from 7.6% in July to 7.3%), which fits September or October. Emerging-market equity at +8.0% in 1m and developed ex-US at +6.5% are consistent with October 2013, when the S&P rose 4.6%. Here US large-cap is only +2.8% over 1m, which is closer to November 2013 (+3.0%). Gold in November 2013 fell about 6%, which fits the -5.7%. However, EM equity rose in October and fell in November, so the EM figure points to October.

The 7-10y Treasury 1m return of +1.7% fits October, when yields fell. US large-cap +2.8% fits September 2013 (+3.1%) better than October. In September, gold fell about 5%, EM rose about 5%, and 10-year Treasuries gained as the Fed declined to taper. Unemployment was 7.3% in the September report. The 3m equity return of +4.6% fits end-September (July through September, about +5%). The 12m return of +19.8% also fits September 2013 (about +19.3%).

I'll go with September 2013.
